parsed.explanation: The state/province is locally protective: explicit gender-identity discrimination coverage, no facility ban, open state ID markers, sanctuary-city care shielding, and a low-risk assessment. But the visitor first passes through the national regime, which governs passports, visas, entry screening, national facilities and immigration custody. National rules restrict sex markers, can refuse or scrutinise document discrepancies, expose travellers to possible fraud findings, bar trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity, and document severe abuse in immigration custody. Local protections cannot override those national exposures. A trans adult alone or with a minor therefore faces an elevated-risk combined regime: strong after entry in much of daily life, but serious border, facility and custody exposure that the state/province cannot cure.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require M/F sex assigned at birth; X markers no longer issued for new national documents; screening may refuse or demand evidence where documents or appearance raise doubt; suspected misrepresentation can support a permanent fraud finding. Advisories and detentions of trans travellers are reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud findings are not automatic and require four elements with limited waiver; litigation is ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: National border screening overrides state/province protections; state ID openness cannot cure a foreign passport or visa mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections policies include conversion-style practices and denial of care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Fraud findings are not automatic; some national orders have been enjoined; no visitor-specific consular safeguard is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Local sanctuary limits local enforcement but not national immigration custody; a border discrepancy can move a visitor into national detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching gender identity; national buildings and airports are exposure points. Many states/provinces have facility bans, but not this one.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no facility ban; city ordinances require gender-neutral bathrooms and protect nonbinary people; state anti-discrimination covers services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facilities follow the national order; state/local facilities follow protective local rules. A visitor crosses both systems.

care_services.exposure: National measures target minor gender-affirming care, funding, insurance and school transition support; proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming surgery is lawful in the state/province; no adult care prohibition appears; city sanctuary order shields care seekers; anti-discrimination applies.
care_services.interaction: National funding and insurance rules may reach nationally funded programmes; local sanctuary only limits local resources.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups as a priority; a justice-department reward memo mentions 'radical gender ideology'; national orders target school transition support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo does not make gender ideology a criterion; the strategy says mere disagreement will not be targeted; courts have blocked some orders; state is graded low-risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat rhetoric can embolden hostility, but state enforcement and commission protections remain; no local targeting pattern is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order threatens prosecution of teachers using preferred names or pronouns; minor care bans exist in many states/provinces; national insurance restrictions proposed. State school-sports bills target youth but are not enacted.
minors_guardians.protection: This state/province has no facility ban; city ordinances protect youth-serving organisations and require gender-neutral bathrooms; local sanctuary and anti-discrimination apply.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces national border and school/care rhetoric, but local protections apply after entry; border documents remain national.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The state/province hate-crime statute does not cover anti-LGBTQ bias; no statewide hate-crime provision reaches such violence. No documented local pattern of anti-trans violence by police or public is given.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; state human-relations commission investigates discrimination and awards remedies; local ordinances add protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: National hate-crime recourse may apply, but the state hate-crime gap leaves local response uneven; low-risk assessment and no documented police targeting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National rules are in litigation; which measures are operative may vary. State statutory gender-identity guarantee is not codified; hate-crime reinstatement unresolved; sports bills pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Commission interpretation and regulations enforce discrimination bans; courts have enjoined some national orders; city sanctuary order; legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies exist but cannot override national border, facility or custody rules; outcomes depend on which national measures are in force.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve document-mismatch entry scrutiny. The anchor denies entry without detention; this regime adds possible national immigration detention, facility exclusion and custody abuse, though local protections are stronger. The combined operative exposure is lower than the anchor.

The anchor's local protection eventually works after delay with no detention. Here local protections also work after entry, but national border screening, facility exclusion and custody exposure are not mitigated by state law, placing it below the anchor.

The anchor shows a privacy directive operating in a clinic. This state/province has comparable local anti-discrimination and sanctuary protections, but the national entry, facilities and custody regime prevents comparable overall safety, so it rates materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Locally, the state/province is among the more protective environments: gender-identity discrimination coverage, no facility ban, open state ID markers, adult care lawful, local sanctuary and commission enforcement. Those protections operate only after entry and within state/local jurisdiction. The traveller still passes through national passport, visa and entry screening, where sex-marker rules and discrepancy scrutiny can lead to refusal, invasive questioning, possible fraud findings or immigration detention. National facility rules and documented immigration-custody abuse are not cancelled by local law. The result is a mixed regime: low everyday risk in much of the state/province, but serious traveller-facing exposure at the national layer.
